content.tldr: Authentication verifies who you are, whereas authorization determines what resources and actions you are permitted to access.
content.simple_explanation: Authentication (AuthN) validates identity claims through credentials, passwords, biometric scans, or cryptographic tokens (answering 'Who are you?'). Once identity is verified, Authorization (AuthZ) evaluates access control policies (Role-Based Access Control RBAC, Attribute-Based Access Control ABAC) to determine whether that authenticated identity has permission to execute specific actions (answering 'What are you allowed to do?').
content.real_world_example: An airport boarding gate: presenting your government passport authenticates your identity as a verified traveler; checking your boarding pass ticket authorizes you to board flight 402 and sit in seat 14B.
content.why_it_matters_and_pitfalls: Conflating AuthN and AuthZ leads to Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) vulnerabilities: an application authenticates that User A is valid, but fails to authorize whether User A is allowed to view User B's billing records (`/api/invoices/1029`).
